snippet.title: What a powerful Pacific Ocean earthquake could mean for Oregon 〰️
snippet.description:
An 8.8-magnitude earthquake struck off the coast of Russia Tuesday, sending waves rushing towards Japan, Hawaii, and the West Coast of the U.S. It was one of the biggest earthquakes ever recorded. 

Seismologists say there’s a 37% chance of a similar size or even bigger earthquake hitting the Pacific Northwest in the next 50 years — what’s become known as the Cascadia Subduction Zone earthquake, or “The Big One.”

So why are there all these tsunamis in the Pacific, and what would it mean for the Pacific Northwest? OPB dove into the history of these dangerous quakes and explored how tsunamis work in the documentary “Unprepared.” 

You can watch the full doc here: https://watch.opb.org/video/oregon-field-guide-unprepared-oregon-field-guide-special/

snippet.description:
Tuesday's magnitude 8.8 earthquake in Russia served as a stark reminder of the seismic risks faced by residents in quake-prone regions, including the Pacific Northwest.

Alerts were issued up and down the Washington coast, and the public responded promptly. Vasily Titov, a research oceanographer at the Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory at NOAA, expressed satisfaction with the system's performance during the event.

Titov noted that the recent tsunami in Kamchatka served as a valuable test case.

snippet.title: The 10 Survival Gears Every American Should Own Before WW3 Starts!
snippet.description:
A 72-hour emergency can expose the gaps in even a well-prepared household. These 10 emergency preparedness essentials can help you prepare before the next blackout, winter storm, or major disruption.

From emergency water storage and backup power to first aid, communication, and shelter, every item serves a practical purpose.

Learn how to build a realistic emergency kit, organize a 72-hour survival plan, and identify the supplies your household may be missing.

Which of these essentials would you need most if the power went out tonight? Watch through number one and check your own setup.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN

- How to prepare a basic emergency communication kit.
- Which tools and repair supplies belong in your household kit.
- How to plan for cold weather, exposure, and temporary shelter.
- Why water storage and appropriate purification methods matter.
- What to include in a first-aid kit and why training matters.
- How to prepare lighting and backup power without relying on one device.
- Important safety rules for emergency cooking, generators, and carbon monoxide.
- Why paper maps and alternate routes are useful when navigation systems fail.
- How to assemble a practical go-bag for the first 72 hours of an emergency.

BUILD YOUR 72-HOUR EMERGENCY PLAN

Start with the needs of everyone in your household, including children, older family members, pets, and anyone who depends on medication or powered medical equipment. Store essential supplies where you can find them, check expiration dates, and review your plan regularly.

Emergency preparedness is not about predicting a particular disaster. It is about making practical decisions before an emergency leaves you without electricity, communication, transportation, or access to nearby stores.

Which item are you missing: water, first aid, lighting, backup power, communication, or a complete go-bag?

Share your answer in the comments, and subscribe for more practical survival skills, emergency planning, outdoor knowledge, and preparedness gear breakdowns.
